title: Selecting Correction Terms for Uniform Threshold Implementations
summary: Correction terms can change uniformity while correctness and non-completeness remain unchanged, but a method that avoids exhaustive search for large functions remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a non-uniform threshold implementation of a large nonlinear Boolean function, find a method for selecting and combining correction terms so that the resulting implementation is uniform while correctness and non-completeness remain unchanged. The method should avoid exhaustive examination of all candidate correction terms and their combinations, which is infeasible for large functions.

scope.domain: Threshold implementations of large nonlinear Boolean functions, focusing on achieving uniformity through correction terms.
parameters: Boolean function size: the large-function regime
correction terms: candidates to select and combine
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a method for selecting and combining correction terms to obtain uniformity while keeping correctness and non-completeness unchanged, without exhaustively examining all candidate terms and combinations for large functions.

citations.label: The First Thorough Side-Channel Hardware Trojan

progress.summary: The source explains that adding correction terms changes the design's uniformity without altering correctness and non-completeness, while exhaustive examination of all terms and combinations is infeasible for large functions. It leaves the method for obtaining a uniform construction unresolved.
citation_labels: Maik Ender et al., The First Thorough Side-Channel Hardware Trojan
